entries.title: Application crashed
entries.what: A program closed unexpectedly. The faulting module tells where it crashed: the program itself, a Windows DLL, or a third-party add-on.
causes: Third-party DLL injected into the program (antivirus, overlays, shell extensions)
Bad RAM if many unrelated programs crash
fix: Update or reinstall the program
If the faulting module belongs to another product (overlay, antivirus, plugin), update or remove that product
Install the latest Visual C++ / .NET runtimes
Many different programs crashing = test RAM and run sfc /scannow

entries.title: Program could not access a file
entries.what: Windows could not access a file needed by a program and closed it (often a network or removable drive).
causes: Program run from a network share or USB drive that disconnected
fix: Run the program from a local disk; check the network/drive

entries.title: Application stopped responding
entries.what: A program hung and was closed (by the user or by Windows).
causes: Waiting for a slow network share or disk
fix: Update the program
Check whether it was waiting on a network drive or printer
If frequent, check disk health

entries.title: Error report (fault bucket)
entries.what: Windows Error Reporting recorded details about a crash or hang that happened right before. Look at the related crash event.

entries.title: .NET application crashed
entries.what: A .NET program crashed with an unhandled exception. The message contains the exception type and stack trace.
fix: Send the exception text to the vendor; update the program

entries.title: .NET application terminated itself
entries.what: A .NET program requested immediate termination (FailFast), usually after detecting a fatal error.
fix: Update the program

entries.title: .NET fatal execution engine error
entries.what: The .NET runtime itself hit a fatal error.
fix: Repair/reinstall .NET
Update the program

entries.title: Profiler attach infrastructure failed (harmless)
entries.what: A .NET Framework process could not initialize the profiler-attach channel, typically because it runs under a restricted account. Developer diagnostics only; has no effect on the program.
causes: Service running as a restricted account (LocalService, sandbox)
fix: Safe to ignore

entries.title: Program could not start: missing runtime
entries.what: Windows could not build the runtime environment for a program - usually a missing Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable.
causes: Visual C++ Redistributable missing or damaged
fix: Install the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributables (x86 and x64)
Reinstall the program

entries.title: Program installed
entries.what: Windows Installer completed an installation successfully.

entries.title: Program installation failed
entries.what: A Windows Installer installation failed.
fix: Run the installer with logging: msiexec /i package.msi /l*v install.log
Look for 'Return value 3' in the log

entries.title: Program removed
entries.what: Windows Installer removed a program.

entries.title: Installation finished
entries.what: Windows Installer finished installing a product. Status 0 = success.

entries.title: Program removal finished
entries.what: Windows Installer finished removing a product. Status 0 = success.

entries.title: Program reconfigured
entries.what: Windows Installer reconfigured (repaired/changed) a product.

entries.title: Installer transaction begin/end
entries.what: Windows Installer started or ended a transaction. Harmless.

entries.title: Installer detected a missing component
entries.what: Windows Installer noticed a component was missing and may self-repair. Usually harmless.

entries.title: Installer self-repair check
entries.what: Windows Installer detected a feature to repair. Usually harmless unless it repeats at every program start.

entries.title: Restart Manager session
entries.what: An installer used Restart Manager to close and restart programs during an install. Harmless.

entries.title: Registry file still in use at logoff
entries.what: A program kept the user's registry open at logoff; Windows freed it. Very common and harmless.

entries.title: Logged on with a temporary profile
entries.what: Windows could not load the user's profile and created a temporary one. Changes will be lost at logoff.
fix: Check HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList for a .bak duplicate of the user's SID
Back up data, then fix or recreate the profile

entries.title: Profile loaded from backup
entries.what: Windows backed up and used a copy of the user's profile because the original could not be loaded.
fix: Same as for temporary profiles

entries.title: Could not load user profile registry
entries.what: Windows could not load the user's registry file (NTUSER.DAT).
fix: Restart; if it repeats, repair or recreate the profile

entries.title: Logon failed: profile not found
entries.what: The user could not log on because the profile could not be found or created.
fix: Check C:\Users\Default and permissions

entries.title: Profile notification event
entries.what: A component did not handle a profile notification. Commonly harmless.

entries.title: Folder redirection failed
entries.what: A user folder could not be redirected to its network location.
fix: Check access to the target share

entries.title: Run key command started
entries.what: Explorer started a command from a Run registry key. Harmless.

entries.title: Application blocked shutdown
entries.what: An application prevented Windows from shutting down or kept it waiting.

entries.title: System pop-up message
entries.what: Windows showed a pop-up error message (the text is in the message).

entries.title: Boot performance
entries.what: How long Windows took to start, with details on slow components.

entries.title: Shutdown performance
entries.what: How long Windows took to shut down.

entries.title: Something slowed down startup
entries.what: A program, driver or service made Windows start slower than normal. The message names it.
fix: Update or remove the named component if boot is slow

entries.title: Something slowed down shutdown
entries.what: A service or program made shutdown slower than normal. The message names it.
